summary: Turn medicine consumption and service data into reviewable forecasts and procurement plans. Explore the five-day course and its practical curriculum.
lede: Medicine quantification and forecasting turns consumption, service and morbidity data into product requirements and procurement plans. For quantification officers, procurement planners, pharmacists and programme managers, the course develops skills in checking data quality, calculating requirements with consumption- and morbidity-based methods, and reconciling stock on hand, confirmed orders and lead times. Practical exercises use Excel to draft procurement plans and review stock-out or overstocking risks.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who prepare or review medicine and health-commodity forecasts, especially when service data, stock records and procurement timelines need to be reconciled.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with essential medicines or health commodities and routine consumption, service or stock information is recommended. No coding or programming is required. Bring a laptop with access to Excel or an equivalent spreadsheet application; no additional software installation is required.
